title: Class 4 consists of simple localized structures interacting in complex ways

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Class 4 consists of simple localized structures interacting in complex ways

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Class 4 cellular automata mix order and randomness: they produce localized structures that are individually fairly simple, but which move around and interact with each other in very complicated ways.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: class 4 involves a mixture of order and randomness: localized structures are produced which on their own are fairly simple, but these structures move around and interact with each other in very complicated ways.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Four Classes of Behavior” (from p. 231), p. 235. Scope: class 4 cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Localized objects and interactions can be quantified in known class 4 systems with existing simulations. Because the claim partly defines the informal class and generalizes over it, evidence is strong but not fully discriminating.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a preregistered set of class 4 rules, detect bounded coherent structures, track their velocities, and quantify collision outcome diversity and background entropy. Compare these metrics with class 2 and class 3 controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Class 4 membership and “very complicated” are partly subjective.

Structure detectors can be rule-specific.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.7
data existence: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Named exemplars such as rule 110 have public simulators and, for Life, a public object census, so the phenomenology of simple objects with long collisions can be checked directly. The class label in the sentence is itself assigned by that phenomenology, which limits how far the check can discriminate a rival description. The result is a solid audit of exemplars and a weak test of the class as a class.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For rule 110 and other rules already tagged class 4 by an independent activity criterion, catalogue persistent finite objects and measure collision transients. Simple periodic objects whose collisions have long, input-sensitive transients support the description for those rules.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fairly simple and very complicated are not numeric.

Localized interacting structures are the visual mark already used to name class 4.

Object censuses cover famous rules and miss an open-ended class.
